text: You are the children of the LORD your God. Do not cut yourselves or shave the front of your heads for the dead,
for you are a people holy to the LORD your God. Out of all the peoples on the face of the earth, the LORD has chosen you to be his treasured people.
You must not eat anything detestable.
These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the sheep, the goat,
the deer, the gazelle, the roebuck, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.
You may eat any animal that has a divided hoof, split in two, and that chews the cud.
But these you must not eat, though they chew the cud or have a divided hoof: the camel, the hare, and the rock badger. They chew the cud but do not have divided hooves; they are unclean for you.
The pig, too, is unclean for you, because it has a divided hoof but does not chew the cud. You must not eat their meat or touch their carcasses.
Of all that lives in the water you may eat this: whatever has fins and scales you may eat.
But whatever has no fins and scales you must not eat; it is unclean for you.
You may eat any clean bird.
But these you must not eat: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
the buzzard, the falcon, any kind of kite,
any kind of raven,
the ostrich, the nighthawk, the sea gull, any kind of hawk,
the little owl, the great owl, the white owl,
the pelican, the carrion vulture, the cormorant,
the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
All winged insects that swarm are unclean for you; do not eat them.
You may eat any clean winged creature.

versions.text: But you may eat any clean bird.
versions.explanation: Verse 11 uses Hebrew tsippor ("bird") while verse 20 uses 'oph ("winged creature"). Rendering both identically makes the chapter sound repetitive when read aloud and loses the distinction; the added "But" also has no basis in the Hebrew, which is a simple positive summary statement.

text: Do not eat anything you find already dead. You may give it to the foreigner residing in your towns, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to an outsider. But you are a people holy to the LORD your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
Be sure to set aside a tenth of all that your fields produce each year.

Eat the tithe of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks in the presence of the LORD your God at the place he will choose as a dwelling for his Name, so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God always.
But if the place the LORD your God chooses to put his Name is too far away, and the journey is too great for you to carry your tithe—because the LORD your God has blessed you—
then exchange it for silver, take the silver in your hand, and go to the place the LORD your God chooses.
Use the silver to buy whatever you desire: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink—whatever you wish. Then you and your household shall eat there in the presence of the LORD your God and rejoice.
And do not neglect the Levite living in your towns, for he has no portion or inheritance of his own among you.
At the end of every three years, bring out all the tithe of that year's produce and store it in your towns,

so that the Levite, who has no portion or inheritance among you, and the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow who live in your towns may come and eat their fill. Then the LORD your God will bless you in all the work of your hands that you undertake.

versions.text: so that the Levite, who has no portion or inheritance among you, and the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow who live in your towns may come and eat their fill. Then the LORD your God will bless you in all the work of your hands.
versions.explanation: The closing Hebrew phrase asher ta'aseh ("that you do/undertake") is omitted. Restoring it completes the sense and gives the sentence a fuller cadence for oral reading.
